name: Technical University of Munich
overview: Germany's highest-ranked technical university. Important for non-EU applicants: TUM reintroduced tuition from winter semester 2024/25, so a Bangladeshi student pays roughly 2,000-3,000 EUR per semester for a bachelor's and 4,000-6,000 EUR per semester for a master's, plus the semester fee. Germany is not tuition-free here.

name: RWTH Aachen University
overview: One of Europe's largest engineering faculties, in North Rhine-Westphalia, which charges no general tuition to non-EU students. Costs are limited to the semester contribution of about 375 EUR, which includes a transport pass covering the Aachen region and cross-border travel into Belgium and the Netherlands.

name: Technical University of Berlin
overview: A leading technical university in a comparatively affordable capital city. Berlin charges no tuition to non-EU students; the semester contribution of roughly 320 EUR includes the VBB Semesterticket covering all Berlin and Brandenburg public transport.

name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
overview: Bavaria's largest comprehensive university, strong in medicine, natural sciences, law and the humanities. Unlike TUM, LMU had not introduced non-EU tuition at the time of recording, leaving only the semester contribution - confirm against the programme page before advising a student.

name: Heidelberg University
overview: Germany's oldest university and a research powerhouse in medicine and the life sciences. It sits in Baden-Wurttemberg, which charges non-EU students 1,500 EUR per semester - about 3,000 EUR a year - on top of the semester contribution.

name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
overview: A combined university and national research centre, particularly strong in mechanical engineering, informatics and energy. Baden-Wurttemberg's non-EU tuition of 1,500 EUR per semester applies.

name: University of Stuttgart
overview: An engineering-led university embedded in Germany's automotive and manufacturing heartland, with close industry links for theses and internships. Baden-Wurttemberg's non-EU tuition of 1,500 EUR per semester applies.

name: TU Dresden
overview: A broad technical university in Saxony with a notably low cost of living by German standards. Saxony charges no general tuition to non-EU students, leaving only the semester contribution.

name: Humboldt University of Berlin
overview: A research university with exceptional standing in the humanities, social sciences and theoretical disciplines. No tuition for non-EU students; the Berlin semester contribution applies.

name: University of Freiburg
overview: A comprehensive research university in south-west Germany with well-established English-taught master's programmes in the environmental and life sciences. Baden-Wurttemberg's non-EU tuition of 1,500 EUR per semester applies.
